The evidence can't answer this for 2026. The data series ends in 2025 (annual, 2001–2025), so nothing in 2026 was observed.

For the period it does cover, 2021–2025, no tree-cover loss event of 0.5 ha or more was detected across the property (374.8 ha). Valid observations covered 100% of the asset. About 43.3 ha (11.55%) was forest in 2020 according to the JRC reference map.

Limits on that result:
- Changes smaller than 0.5 ha, at edges, or narrower than the 30 m pixels may have been missed, so it doesn't prove there was no change at all.
- It isn't a regulatory or compliance finding (e.g., EUDR).
- It says nothing about anything outside 2021–2025.

To assess 2026, you'd need the next annual data release or another source covering that year.
